title: An HPC-Inspired Blueprint for a Technology-Agnostic Quantum Middle Layer
problem: Quantum software must be rewritten for different quantum backends (gate-based, annealing, CV)
motivation: Lack of portable quantum middleware; need for hardware-agnostic abstraction similar to HPC libraries
method: The approach creates a translation layer between quantum programs and different quantum hardware types. It works by splitting the problem into two parts: intent (the computation you want to perform) stays separate from context (the description tailored for a specific quantum backend type, like gate-based Qiskit or annealing D-Wave systems). A working example built with Qiskit and D-Wave demonstrates that programs written in this middle layer can run on different quantum hardware types without being rewritten.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using a backend-neutral middle layer that separates intent from context with a descriptor pattern (borrowed from high-performance computing design), so quantum code only needs to be written once regardless of which quantum hardware it runs on.
contributions: Typed intent + context descriptor separation model
Demonstration on two distinct quantum paradigms (gate-model, annealing)
